title: Oven Roasted Portuguese Cheese Flatbread
description: A sweet, flaky brunch‑mood Portuguese dish featuring cheese slices and a mortar‑pestle‑pound dough, shojin‑friendly.
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine flour, yeast, sugar, and salt.
Warm the milk to 110°F (43°C) and pour into the dry mixture, stirring until a shaggy dough forms.
Add melted butter and honey, then knead the dough on a lightly floured surface for about 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm spot for 60 minutes, or until doubled in size.
Punch down the dough and divide it into 2 equal portions, shaping each into a round flatbread about 1/4 inch thick.
Place the flatbreads on a parchment‑lined baking sheet, brush the tops with beaten egg, and sprinkle with chopped rosemary.
Arrange the cheese slices on each flatbread, slightly overlapping, and fold the edges over to create a pocket.
Bake in a preheated oven at 375°F (190°C) for 15 minutes, or until golden brown and the cheese is melted.
Remove the flatbread from the oven, let rest for 5 minutes, then slice into wedges and serve warm.
Optionally dust with a light drizzle of honey or a sprinkle of powdered sugar for extra sweetness.
